parameters.content:
## Store 6 · Slack command

One slash command for the whole store.

- `/store` or `/store help`: the commands and every job, by phase.
- `/store status`: what's waiting for a decision in every review queue (the `store_queues` view), with a link to the review page.
- `/store page` or `/store page <queue>`: a private link to the review page, signed for `link_hours`.
- `/store run <job>`: starts that job now, the same as its schedule would (`/store run pricing decide`, `/store run images find`). `/store run setup` runs every Setup lane, one after another.

Every request is checked against Slack's signature. With `approver_ids` set, only those people can run jobs or open the page; everyone else gets a polite no. Slack wants an answer within three seconds, so `run` answers first, then starts the jobs and replies again with what started.

build.py writes `jobs` from each template's lanes. **Run the jobs** calls each workflow's **Run from /store** webhook with the **Store run key** header.

nodes.name: Slack sends /store
nodes.notes: The /store command's Request URL (the manifest sets it).

nodes.name: Command settings
nodes.notes: build.py writes jobs and phases. approver_ids: Slack user IDs that may run jobs and open the page (empty = anyone in the workspace).

nodes.name: What to do
nodes.notes: Signature (and app and workspace, when set), then the sub-command.

nodes.name: Sign a page link
nodes.notes: The review page checks the same HMAC, so a link can't be changed or reused after it expires.

nodes.name: Count what's waiting

parameters.query: select queue, label, phase, channel, waiting, oldest from store_queues order by phase, queue

nodes.notes: The store_queues view in schema.sql: one row per review queue.

nodes.name: Say it's starting
nodes.notes: Answers Slack straight away; the jobs start after.

nodes.name: Run the jobs
nodes.notes: Why HTTP: each workflow's Run from /store webhook starts the lane, and answers as soon as it has. Setup lanes go 3 seconds apart.

parameters.query: insert into store_activity (source, user_id, user_name, action, detail) values ('/store', $1, $2, 'run', $3)

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('What to do').first().json.u, $('What to do').first().json.n, $('One item per job').all().map((j, i) => j.json.job + ($('Run the jobs').all()[i]?.json?.error ? ' (failed)' : '')).join(', ') ] }}

nodes.name: Say what started

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (() => { const jobs = $('One item per job').all().map(i => i.json.job); const res = $('Run the jobs').all().map(i => i.json); const failed = jobs.filter((j, i) => res[i]?.error); const started = jobs.filter((j, i) => !res[i]?.error); return JSON.stringify({ response_type: 'ephemeral', text: (started.length ? 'Started ' + started.map(j => '`' + j + '`').join(', ') + '. Each one posts to its own channel when it has something to show.' : '') + (failed.length ? '\n:warning: Could not start ' + failed.map(j => '`' + j + '`').join(', ') + '. Is that workflow published, with the Store run key on its Run from /store node?' : '') }); })() }}

nodes.notes: Why HTTP: Slack's response_url, so the reply lands with the command, privately.
